theses.thesis: NVIDIA will increasingly defend its AI infrastructure position by making NVLink/rack architecture a platform for third-party custom accelerators, not only by selling NVIDIA-designed GPUs.
theses.rationale: NVLink Fusion and the MediaTek partnership pointed toward monetizing interconnect and system architecture even when customers use custom compute dies. The September 9 Qualcomm-Amazon custom-silicon and optical-connectivity collaboration remains counter-pressure. On September 11, d-Matrix became direct supporting evidence: its next-generation Raptor inference XPUs will integrate into NVIDIA rack infrastructure through NVLink Fusion under a multi-year roadmap. This materially strengthens the thesis from a strategy announcement into third-party XPU adoption, although production economics remain unproven.
falsifiers: Major custom-XPU builders broadly reject NVLink Fusion in favor of open/alternative fabrics
NVLink Fusion sees little production adoption outside NVIDIA-centric systems
NVIDIA retreats from third-party XPU integration

evidence_updates.summary: Qualcomm and Amazon announced multi-generation custom AI silicon plus optical interconnect work for AWS, strengthening the competing-platform path NVIDIA must overcome.
NVIDIA Dynamo EPD extended NVIDIA's stack upward into multimodal serving architecture; confidence unchanged.

d-Matrix announced Raptor XPU integration with NVIDIA NVLink Fusion, Vera CPUs, NVLink switches, BlueField-4, ConnectX-9 and Spectrum-X. This is direct third-party accelerator adoption and raises thesis confidence from medium-high to high; production performance remains an open test.

No new independent production-performance evidence on NVLink Fusion or Raptor surfaced in today's window. Thesis remains active with high confidence; production economics are still the key falsification surface.

theses.thesis: By March 2027, at least two major frontier or enterprise AI platforms will expose customer-configurable runtime policies plus customer-controlled agent telemetry as first-class product primitives rather than keeping these controls only as vendor-internal safety systems.
theses.rationale: OpenAI pairs advanced capability with gated access and runtime monitoring; Anthropic is moving monitoring data into customer-controlled clouds; Microsoft productizes agent identity and tool policy; Meta Muse externalizes credentials and egress; Red Hat AI 3.5 adds guardrails/observability. September 11 added an NPCI registry signal and orchestration-focused threat intelligence. September 12 added RubyGems, Beltdown and OpenAI Habitat as evidence that prompt intent and shell isolation are insufficient without whole-runtime capability control. September 13 extends the same architectural lesson into the inference layer: SGLang CVE-2026-86793 shows why administrative model/weight mutation endpoints, authentication and deserialization boundaries are part of the operational control plane. This supports the direction of the thesis without yet satisfying its two-platform customer-product criterion.
falsifiers: Runtime policy and action monitoring remain mostly vendor-internal across major AI platforms through March 2027
Customer-controlled agent telemetry remains a niche or pilot-only feature without meaningful enterprise production adoption
Major providers retreat toward model-only refusals without exposing operational policy controls

evidence_updates.summary: Meta published Muse's Sentinel/secure-runtime architecture with user-scoped action approvals and egress enforcement. AWS published an AgentCore/GitHub Actions pattern for trace-based regression gates.
Red Hat AI 3.5 positioned guardrails and observability as platform primitives; payment networks converged on agent identity and delegated intent.

NPCI reportedly plans an AI-agent registry for UPI and Anthropic's new threat-intelligence reporting highlights cross-session orchestration as a detection target. Thesis remains active with high confidence.

RubyGems/OpenAI and the Beltdown disclosure add concrete evidence that prompt intent and shell sandboxing are insufficient without whole-runtime capability control. OpenAI Habitat independently demonstrates central access-policy/audit enforcement as a production systems pattern. Confidence remains high.

SGLang CVE-2026-86793 expands the hard-boundary requirement into inference administration: mutation endpoints, authentication and serialization format are part of the same external control-plane problem. Confidence remains high; this is architectural support, not yet evidence that two major platforms expose the thesis's customer-facing primitives.
